subsystems.name: Design engine
subsystems.role: invents a protein shape and sequence that does a chosen job.
parts: physics-based sequence scoring and stability simulation

subsystems.name: Gene synthesis and assembly
subsystems.role: turns the digital design into a physical gene.
parts: enzymatic assembly into an expression plasmid

subsystems.name: Expression host
subsystems.role: reads the gene and makes the protein.
parts: engineered CHO or HEK293 mammalian cells
E. coli or yeast for simpler proteins

subsystems.name: Purification and analytics
subsystems.role: separates the wanted protein from everything else and proves it is correct.

subsystems.name: Formulation and delivery
subsystems.role: keeps the protein stable and gets it to the right tissue.
parts: pre-filled syringes, or lipid nanoparticles and mRNAs for in-body production

subsystems.name: Immunogenicity and safety assessment
subsystems.role: checks the body will not attack or over-react to a non-natural protein.

buildSteps.title: Define the job
buildSteps.detail: Pick the exact molecular target or reaction the protein must perform, such as blocking one receptor or catalysing one bond.

buildSteps.title: Generate candidate scaffolds
buildSteps.detail: Generative design software proposes hundreds of backbone shapes that could present the right binding surface or active site; this step existed only on paper before the 2020s.

buildSteps.title: Design sequences
buildSteps.detail: For each backbone, software chooses the amino acid at every position to fold correctly and bind tightly, then filters out sequences likely to aggregate or provoke an immune response.

buildSteps.title: Verify in silico
buildSteps.detail: Folding-prediction models re-check that the designed sequence would actually adopt the intended shape before any lab work.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the genes
buildSteps.detail: The chosen sequences are written as DNA by commercial synthesis, then inserted into an expression plasmid.

buildSteps.title: Express the protein
buildSteps.detail: Cells in a bioreactor grow for days to weeks, secreting or accumulating the protein; simple designs may instead be made in bacteria or in cell-free reactions.

buildSteps.title: Purify and characterise
buildSteps.detail: Chromatography steps isolate the protein, and mass spectrometry, stability tests and binding assays confirm it is the molecule that was designed.

buildSteps.title: Optimise by directed evolution
buildSteps.detail: Libraries of variants are displayed on yeast or phage surfaces, and the best binders are selected and re-tested — often several rounds.

buildSteps.title: Test and scale up
buildSteps.detail: Lead candidates go through preclinical safety and efficacy studies, then manufacturing is scaled to clinical-grade bioreactors.

prerequisites.why: knowing the shape a sequence will fold into is what makes design computational rather than trial-and-error.
designers must build and test many variants, so each gene has to cost little.
complex human-like proteins need cell culture, purification and quality control at industrial scale.
designed proteins are rarely good enough first time and must be evolved in the lab.
most proteins cannot cross a cell membrane, so intracellular targets remain out of reach for injected biologics.
an engineered protein can still trigger an immune response, and current screens only partly predict it.

pathway.milestone: engineered antibodies, Fc-fusion proteins, enzyme-replacement drugs and cell therapies are routinely used in the clinic
pathway.unlocks: a proven regulatory and manufacturing base for protein medicines.

pathway.milestone: designed-from-scratch binders enter human trials for viral and oncology targets
pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper discovery of molecules that natural proteins cannot provide.

pathway.milestone: mRNA-delivered synthetic proteins produced inside the patient, and designed proteins that hit intracellular targets
pathway.unlocks: treatment of diseases currently considered undruggable.

pathway.milestone: modular design platforms plus rapid synthesis and manufacturing
pathway.unlocks: response to new pathogens in weeks, and small-batch personalised protein therapies.
